items.stem: In June 1898, opponents of annexing the Philippines founded an organization in Boston to carry the non-imperialists' case to the American public. What was that organization called?
items.stemEs: En junio de 1898, los opositores a la anexión de Filipinas fundaron en Boston una organización para presentar al público estadounidense los argumentos de los antiimperialistas. ¿Cómo se llamaba esa organización?

choices.textEs: La Liga de Restricción a la Inmigración
choices.explanation: A real Boston organization founded in 1894, and it shared several members with the anti-annexation campaign. Its subject was who could enter the United States, not whether the United States should govern territory overseas.
choices.misconception: treats any Boston reform league of the 1890s as the anti-annexation organization

choices.explanation: A real nativist order founded in 1887, directed against Catholic immigrants and their influence in city politics. It took no position on the Philippines.
choices.misconception: reads any organization of the period with a patriotic-sounding name as part of the imperialism debate

choices.explanation: A real organization, but founded in 1900 — two years after the date in the question — and created to mediate between organized labour and employers.
choices.misconception: accepts an organization founded after the event it is said to have responded to

items.dokRationale: Recall of a named organization and its founding year. The student retrieves one fact; no comparison of arguments, period placement or inference is required. A DOK 2 item on this standard would require one of the three.
items.explanation: The Anti-Imperialist League gave a scattered opposition a single platform and a membership list that crossed party, class and region — which is why the arguments it published can be set beside the imperialists' as one side of a debate rather than as isolated complaints.
items.explanationEs: La Liga Antiimperialista dio a una oposición dispersa una sola plataforma y una lista de miembros que cruzaba partidos, clases y regiones; por eso sus argumentos publicados pueden ponerse junto a los de los imperialistas como un bando de un debate y no como quejas aisladas.

items.stem: Non-imperialists argued that governing Filipinos without their consent contradicted the Declaration of Independence. Which statement best describes the answer imperialists most often gave to that objection?
items.stemEs: Los antiimperialistas sostenían que gobernar a los filipinos sin su consentimiento contradecía la Declaración de Independencia. ¿Qué afirmación describe mejor la respuesta que los imperialistas daban con mayor frecuencia a esa objeción?

choices.text: The Filipinos were not yet capable of self-government, so American rule was a trusteeship preparing them for it.
choices.textEs: Los filipinos aún no eran capaces de gobernarse, por lo que el dominio estadounidense era una tutela que los preparaba para ello.

choices.text: The Constitution did not reach of its own force into territory the United States had acquired but never incorporated into the Union.
choices.textEs: La Constitución no llegaba por sí misma a un territorio que Estados Unidos había adquirido pero nunca incorporado a la Unión.
choices.explanation: A real argument and a successful one — the Supreme Court adopted it in the Insular Cases, beginning with Downes v. Bidwell in 1901. It is an answer about which constitutional provisions follow the flag, made in the courts after annexation, and it concedes the consent objection rather than meeting it.
choices.misconception: mistakes a legal argument about where the Constitution applies for a moral argument about who may be governed

choices.text: The Teller Amendment had already disclaimed any American intention of annexing the islands.
choices.textEs: La Enmienda Teller ya había rechazado toda intención estadounidense de anexar las islas.
choices.explanation: True of Cuba and of nothing else. The Teller Amendment of April 1898 disclaimed any intention to annex CUBA, and that promise was kept. It said nothing about the Philippines, which the Treaty of Paris ceded outright.
choices.misconception: carries the Cuban promise over to the Philippines and treats one island's terms as the terms of the whole war

choices.text: The Treaty of Paris itself promised eventual independence, so the question of consent did not arise.
choices.textEs: El Tratado de París mismo prometía la independencia eventual, por lo que la cuestión del consentimiento no se planteaba.
choices.explanation: The Treaty of Paris of December 1898 ceded the Philippines to the United States for $20 million and promised nothing about independence. A promised date did not arrive until the Tydings-McDuffie Act of 1934.
choices.misconception: moves a promise made in 1934 back into the treaty that started the argument

items.dokRationale: The student must hold both sides' arguments at once and judge which of four real period positions actually meets the consent objection rather than sidestepping it. Recalling that imperialists favoured annexation would not answer it.
items.explanation: Imperialists did not deny the principle of consent; they deferred it. Framing American rule as a temporary tutelage let them claim the Declaration for their own side, which is why the two camps could quote the same document against each other.
items.explanationEs: Los imperialistas no negaban el principio del consentimiento: lo posponían. Presentar el dominio estadounidense como una tutela temporal les permitía reclamar la Declaración para su propio bando, y por eso ambos campos podían citar el mismo documento uno contra otro.

items.stem: Andrew Carnegie, Samuel Gompers and Senator Benjamin Tillman all opposed annexing the Philippines. Which statement best explains why the non-imperialists are better described as a coalition than as one movement?
items.stemEs: Andrew Carnegie, Samuel Gompers y el senador Benjamin Tillman se opusieron todos a la anexión de Filipinas. ¿Qué afirmación explica mejor por qué a los antiimperialistas se les describe mejor como una coalición que como un solo movimiento?

choices.text: All three rested their objection on the consent-of-the-governed clause of the Declaration of Independence, which the Anti-Imperialist League's platform of 1899 made its central charge against the war in the Philippines.
choices.textEs: Los tres basaban su objeción en la cláusula del consentimiento de los gobernados de la Declaración de Independencia, que la plataforma de la Liga Antiimperialista de 1899 convirtió en su acusación central contra la guerra en Filipinas.
choices.explanation: The League's platform did make that charge, and some of its members believed it. These three did not all share it: Gompers argued from wage competition and Tillman from race. Taking the platform as every member's reasoning is what hides the coalition.
choices.misconception: reads an organization's published platform as the belief of each person who signed it

choices.text: Opposition was a Democratic Party position, since William Jennings Bryan made it the paramount issue of the 1900 presidential campaign.
choices.textEs: La oposición era una posición del Partido Demócrata, ya que William Jennings Bryan la convirtió en el tema primordial de la campaña presidencial de 1900.
choices.explanation: Bryan did run on it in 1900, so the second half is true. The League was deliberately bipartisan and Carnegie was a Republican; Bryan himself had urged Senate Democrats to ratify the Treaty of Paris first.
choices.misconception: turns a party's campaign plank into the whole of the opposition it borrowed

choices.text: All three wanted the islands annexed but governed as a territory rather than admitted as a state.
choices.textEs: Los tres querían que las islas fueran anexadas pero gobernadas como territorio en lugar de admitidas como estado.
choices.explanation: That is what happened, and it is close to what annexation's supporters wanted. It is the position these three men were arguing against, handed to them.
choices.misconception: gives the outcome of the debate to the side that lost it

choices.text: Their reasons conflicted — anti-militarism, wage competition, and refusal to admit non-white peoples — so they agreed on the outcome, not the principle.
choices.textEs: Sus razones se contradecían — antimilitarismo, temor a la competencia salarial y rechazo a incorporar pueblos no blancos a la nación — de modo que coincidían en el resultado y no en el principio.

items.dokRationale: The student is given three names and must infer what the grouping conceals: agreement on an outcome produced by incompatible reasons. Naming each man's position is recall; recognising that the agreement was shallow is the inference the item requires.
items.explanation: A coalition is held together by a shared conclusion, not a shared premise. Reading these three men's reasons side by side also explains why the opposition did not outlast the vote: nothing in it bound an industrialist, a labour leader and a segregationist senator together once annexation was settled.
items.explanationEs: Una coalición se mantiene unida por una conclusión compartida, no por una premisa compartida. Leer juntas las razones de estos tres hombres explica también por qué la oposición no sobrevivió a la votación: nada en ella unía a un industrial, a un dirigente sindical y a un senador segregacionista una vez decidida la anexión.
